correctness.rationale: With y=x exp(z/(2ℓ)) and C=yW, the forward ODE becomes y²W''+yW'−(y²+1)W=0. Only K₁ satisfies decay, and (yK₁)'=−yK₀ ensures decreasing positive C and gives U=√(D₀k)F(x), F=K₀/K₁∈(0,1). The water-side correction is exactly T=k_m v/(k_m−v)=θU; positive finite parameters require 0<v<k_m. The Riccati equation gives E=xF'/F=1+x(F−1/F) and E'=2F+x(F²−F⁻²)=−H/F². The small-x expansion gives H=x+o(x); the large-x coefficients of F are 1, −1/2, 3/8, −3/8 in successive powers of 1/x, yielding H=1/(2x²)+O(x⁻³). At a zero of H, F'=(1−F²)²/(2F²), which gives H'=−2(1−F²)²/(1+F²)<0. All zeros would cross downward, impossible given positivity at both ends. Thus for r=√(k₂/k₁)>1, the log derivative of R(x)=rF(rx)/F(x) is [E(rx)−E(x)]/x<0; the small-x x log(1/x) behavior and large-x F→1 give the unattained endpoints r² and r. Every corrected ratio inside the open interval gives a unique x, then direct positive reconstruction of D₀ and ℓ from T₁. With only one admissible reading, letting x vary over (0,∞) yields the entire continuous ambiguity family of distinct pairs. The supplied SciPy checker was inspected, not run; its root bracket and tests cover bounded ranges and are not a proof or a universal implementation guarantee.
residual_risks: Exact-data statement for the specified half-line exponential profile with shared parameters and known porosity and transfer coefficient. It gives no noise robustness or practical bracketing guarantee near the open endpoints.
